accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a k-dimensional submanifold of the Euclidean unit ball B^n. Are there topological obstructions to Σ occurring as a free boundary minimal submanifold of B^n, meaning that Σ is minimal and meets the boundary sphere ∂B^n orthogonally along ∂Σ? More specifically, which topological types can occur, and does the answer change depending on whether one allows immersed examples or requires embedded examples? In the especially important case of free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3, does there exist such a surface of genus 1 with exactly one boundary component?

evidence.quote: Open Question 1. Are there any topological obstructions for a k-dimension submanifold Σ to be a free boundary minimal submanifold in Bn? Does it depend on whether Σ is immersed or embedded?
To indicate the subtlety of the question in the free boundary setting, it is yet unknown whether there exists a free boundary minimal surface in B3 with genus 1 and one boundary component.

accepted.question_text: Fix a compact surface Σ with boundary and a positive integer k. For the Steklov eigenvalue problem on Σ, what is the sharp supremum of the scale-invariant quantity σ_k(g)|∂Σ|_g over all smooth Riemannian metrics g on Σ? In addition, is that sharp supremum realized by some smooth metric on Σ, rather than only by a singular or non-attained extremal object?

evidence.quote: Open Question 2 (Fraser-Schoen [30]). For each topological type of Σ, what is the sharp upper bound for σk(g)|∂Σ|g? Is it achieved by a smooth metric on Σ?

accepted.question_text: For the p-width min-max construction in the Euclidean unit ball B^n, let Σ_p denote a smooth embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface and n_p a positive integer such that the p-width satisfies ω_p(B^n) = n_p|Σ_p|. Does the family {Σ_p}_{p∈N} contain infinitely many geometrically distinct hypersurfaces? If it does, must their areas satisfy |Σ_p| → +∞ as p → ∞?

evidence.quote: Open Question 3. Is {Σp}p∈N an infinite set? If so, does |Σp| → +∞ as p → ∞?

accepted.question_text: For sufficiently large genus g, consider the two known families of embedded free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3 with genus g and three boundary components: the desingularization examples Σ_g^{KL} of Kapouleas-Li and the equivariant min-max examples Σ_g^{K} of Ketover. Are these two families actually congruent to one another, meaning that for every sufficiently large g they differ only by a rigid motion of B^3?

evidence.quote: Open Question 4. For all g sufficiently large, are the surfaces ΣKL_g and ΣK_g congruent to each other?

accepted.question_text: In the Euclidean unit 3-ball B^3, is the critical catenoid the unique embedded free boundary minimal annulus, up to rigid motions of B^3? Equivalently, whenever an embedded annulus in B^3 is minimal and meets ∂B^3 orthogonally along its boundary, must it be congruent to the critical catenoid?

evidence.quote: Open Question 5. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions in B3) embedded free boundary minimal annulus in B3?

accepted.question_text: Among immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in the Euclidean unit 3-ball B^3, is the critical catenoid the only example with Morse index 4, up to rigid motions? In other words, if an immersed free boundary minimal surface in B^3 has exactly four independent normal deformations that decrease area to second order, must that surface be congruent to the critical catenoid?

evidence.quote: Open Question 6. Is the critical catenoid the only (up to rigid motions) immersed free boundary minimal surface in B3 with Morse index 4?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in the Euclidean unit ball B^n. Since the coordinate functions restricted to Σ are Steklov eigenfunctions with eigenvalue 1, one always has σ_1(Σ) ≤ 1. Must equality always hold? That is, does every embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface in B^n satisfy σ_1(Σ) = 1 for its first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue?

evidence.quote: Open Question 7. If Σ ⊂ Bn is an embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface, then σ1(Σ) = 1.

accepted.question_text: Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold of the Euclidean unit ball B^n, and let f: B^n → B^n be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is the k-dimensional volume of Σ maximal within its conformal orbit, in the sense that |f(Σ)| ≤ |Σ| for every such conformal map f?

evidence.quote: Open Question 8. Let Σk be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in Bn, and f : Bn → Bn be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is it true that |f(Σ)| ≤ |Σ|?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ^k be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold of the Euclidean unit ball B^n, and let f: B^n → B^n be a conformal diffeomorphism. Is the (k−1)-dimensional boundary volume of ∂Σ maximal within its conformal orbit, in the sense that |f(∂Σ)| ≤ |∂Σ| for every such conformal map f?

evidence.quote: Open Question 9. Let Σk be an immersed free boundary minimal submanifold in Bn. Suppose f : Bn → Bn is a conformal diffeomorphism. Is it true that |f(∂Σ)| ≤ |∂Σ|?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in the Euclidean unit 3-ball B^3 that is not an equatorial disk. Is its area always at least the area of the critical catenoid K? Equivalently, among all non-planar immersed free boundary minimal surfaces in B^3, is the critical catenoid the unique candidate for the smallest possible area?

evidence.quote: Open Question 10. Let Σ2 be an immersed free boundary minimal surface in B3 which is not the equatorial disk. Is it true that |Σ| ≥ |K|?
